questions.q: In those days what happened to Hezekiah?
questions.a: He became very ill and neared death.
Isaiah told Hezekiah that Yahweh said he should set his house in order, because he would die and not live.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah do after receiving Yahweh’s message through Isaiah?
questions.a: He prayed to Yahweh asking Yahweh to remember how he had faithfully walked before Yahweh with his whole heart and how he had done good in Yahweh’s sight. And Hezekiah wept loudly.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Isaiah to say to Hezekiah?
questions.a: He said to tell Hezekiah that he had heard Hezekiah’s prayer and seen his tears. Yahweh told Hezekiah he would add fifteen years to Hezekiah’s life and, in addition, he would rescue Hezekiah and Jerusalem from the king of Assyria and would defend Jerusalem.

questions.q: What sign did Yahweh say he would give so that Hezekiah would know Yahweh would do what he had spoken?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would cause the shadow on the stairs of Ahaz to go back ten steps.

questions.q: In Hezekiah’s written prayer, what did Hezekiah say would happen halfway through his life?
questions.a: He said he would go through the gates of Sheol.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah say about seeing Yah?
questions.a: Hezekiah said he would no longer see Yah in the land of the living.

questions.q: What does Hezekiah pray and ask of God?
questions.a: He tells God he is suffering and he asks for help.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah say to the Lord concerning his sufferings and grief?
questions.a: Hezekiah said the sufferings the Lord sent were good for him and that it was for Hezekiah’s benefit that he experienced such grief.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah say the Lord had done with his sins?
questions.a: Hezekiah said the Lord had thrown all of Hezekiah’s sins behind his back.

questions.q: Does anyone praise or thank God in Sheol?
questions.a: No one praises or thanks God in Sheol.

questions.q: How was Hezekiah going to celebrate Yahweh saving him?
questions.a: Hezekiah said they would celebrate with music all the days of their lives in the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Isaiah say to do so that Hezekiah would recover?
questions.a: Isaiah said they should take a lump of figs and lay it on the boil, and Hezekiah would recover.

commentary.text: Hezekiah's sickness and recovery. (Is. 38:1-8) His thanksgiving. (Is. 38:9-22)

Is. 38:1-8 When we pray in our sickness, though God send not to us such an answer as he here sent to Hezekiah, yet, if by his Spirit he bids us be of good cheer, assures us that our sins are forgiven, and that, whether we live or die, we shall be his, we do not pray in vain. See II Kin. 20:1-11.

Is. 38:9-22 We have here Hezekiah's thanksgiving. It is well for us to remember the mercies we receive in sickness. Hezekiah records the condition he was in. He dwells upon this; I shall no more see the Lord. A good man wishes not to live for any other end than that he may serve God, and have communion with him. Our present residence is like that of a shepherd in his hut, a poor, mean, and cold lodging, and with a trust committed to our charge, as the shepherd has. Our days are compared to the weaver's shuttle, Job 7:6, passing and repassing very swiftly, every throw leaving a thread behind it; and when finished, the piece is cut off, taken out of the loom, and showed to our Master to be judged of. A good man, when his life is cut off, his cares and fatigues are cut off with it, and he rests from his labours. But our times are in God's hand; he has appointed what shall be the length of the piece. When sick, we are very apt to calculate our time, but are still at uncertainty. It should be more our care how we shall get safe to another world. And the more we taste of the loving-kindness of God, the more will our hearts love him, and live to him. It was in love to our poor perishing souls that Christ delivered them. The pardon does not make the sin not to have been sin, but not to be punished as it deserves. It is pleasant to think of our recoveries from sickness, when we see them flowing from the pardon of sin. Hezekiah's opportunity to glorify God in this world, he made the business, and pleasure, and end of life. Being recovered, he resolves to abound in praising and serving God. God's promises are not to do away, but to quicken and encourage the use of means. Life and health are given that we may glorify God and do good.
